cards.explanation: The answer is the LORD and His holy words. The prophet says he's like a drunkard "…because of the LORD, because of His holy words." (Jeremiah 23:9) I think that tells you how heavy those words are to carry. His heart is broken and his bones tremble, and the verse says it's because of the LORD and His holy words.

The answer is True. The prophet says the land is full of adulterers, "…their course is evil and their power is misused." (Jeremiah 23:10) That's a heavy thing to hear, friends. He's not hiding it, and I think that's why his heart is so broken.

The answers are priest and house. The LORD says, "For both prophet and priest are ungodly…" (Jeremiah 23:11) Then He says, "even in My house I have found their wickedness…" The place that belongs to Him is the very place He found it, and I think that tells you how close to home this hits.

The answer is into the darkness. The LORD says, "they will be driven away into the darkness and fall into it." The path is slick, they get pushed along it, and the darkness is where it ends. Not a spot I'd want to be, friends, and I've spent time in the back of a dark drawer.
The answer is True. The LORD says of the prophets of Samaria, "They prophesied by Baal and led My people Israel astray." They weren't just wandering off alone. They pulled His people along with them.
The answer is the hands of evildoers. The LORD says, "They strengthen the hands of evildoers…" Look who they're cheering on. The people who should be calling out wickedness are backing it up instead.

The answer is False. The LORD says the prophets "…strengthen the hands of evildoers, so that no one turns his back on wickedness." (Jeremiah 23:14) Nobody turns his back on it, and I think that's the whole problem here, friends. The people are staying right where they are.
The answer is Sodom. The LORD says, "They are all like Sodom to Me; the people of Jerusalem are like Gomorrah." (Jeremiah 23:14) Two cities named together, and it's a heavy comparison.

The reason is that ungodliness spread from them through the land. The LORD says, "…for from the prophets of Jerusalem ungodliness has spread throughout the land." (Jeremiah 23:15) It spread from them across the land. Wormwood and poisoned water are the heavy consequence He names for it.

The answer is False. The LORD of Hosts says, "Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you." He doesn't want the people hanging on those words. And He tells them why in the next lines.

The answer is from their own minds. The LORD says, "They speak visions from their own minds, not from the mouth of the LORD." It's their own idea, not His word. Friends, it's like a recipe I made up and signed with somebody else's name.

The answer is "No harm will come to you." The LORD says they tell "…everyone who walks in the stubbornness of his own heart, ‘No harm will come to you.’" That's the line. It sounds like comfort, but the LORD says these prophets are not speaking from Him.
The answer is storm. The LORD says, "…the storm of the LORD has gone out with fury, a whirlwind swirling down upon the heads of the wicked." It's moving already, friends. That's serious weather.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "The anger of the LORD will not turn back until He has fully accomplished the purposes of His heart." It doesn't turn around halfway. He finishes what He has set out to do.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "I did not send these prophets, yet they have run with their message; I did not speak to them, yet they have prophesied." They took off running without being sent. And He hadn't spoken to them either.

The answer is that they would have turned His people from their evil ways. The LORD says, "…if they had stood in My council, they would have proclaimed My words to My people and turned them back from their evil ways and deeds." (Jeremiah 23:22) Standing in His council is where proclaiming His words would have come from. And turning His people back is what He says they would have done.
